question: How many languages are there in the 8th schedule of the Indian Constitution as on June 2022?
solution:
The correct answer is __**22 languages**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of June 2022, there are **22 languages** listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Eighth Schedule to the Indian Constitution lists the official languages recognized by the Indian government.
 
• The original constitution included 14 languages in the Eighth Schedule, but several amendments have increased this number to 22.
 
• The languages included are Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri.
 
• Recognition in the Eighth Schedule means that these languages can be used for official purposes such as parliamentary proceedings, judiciary, and communications between the central government and states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Eighth Schedule** of the Constitution has been amended several times to include more languages as per the evolving linguistic diversity of the nation.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The inclusion of languages in the Eighth Schedule is significant for the cultural and linguistic recognition of the diverse population of India.
